title: Arkret Device Key Operation DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.keys.{upload,query,claim}, the Station-to-Station device directory read and ak.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

request_id.description: Client-generated idempotency id. The service keys the canonical request digest and terminal outcome by (account_id, backup_id, request_id).

keys_backups_delete_proof.description: High-risk authority proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1. Exactly one of recovery_unlock, device_quorum or trusted_recovery_service; an ordinary current-device session proof is not accepted for active-series tail deletion.

account_device_key_entries.description: One entry per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id); duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected even when values differ.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ak.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key_did (device-lifecycle.md Ã‚Â§5.2 / Ã‚Â§5.4). To check SignalEnvelope and durable Event proofs, receivers resolve a verification_method DID URL under the verified principal did, validate its bare did through the registered adapter, require project(did) to equal the actor/principal did_core_id, and require its fragment to equal the full ak:device:<uuidv7> id. Constructing a verification method by appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden.

device_generation_state.description: Reducer-managed identity-root generation fence for the principal device directory.

current_device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation; it is not and MUST NOT be derived from a DID versionId.

account_device_generation_entries.description: Current device-generation fence for each exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

device_projection_attestation_core.description: Origin Station assertion that this exact device projection is the account's current accepted one. It is the whole verification closure of the Station-to-Station device directory read and of the account_device signer evidence: the attested body carries no PCR genesis receipt, no device authorization chain and no accepted RealmCommit, because that material is account-internal governance and is disclosed only through ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1 under exact current-holder authorization. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref fields describe the closed shape of a returned usable row; they do not require an unauthorized device to have a partial projection. A device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape. attested_at is a monotone freshness marker and, with authorized_generation_ref, is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3.

account_id.description: Exact account owning the device projection. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto account_id.station_id; an attestation that verifies under any other Station key is not evidence about this account.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence. Security operations use their stricter registered current-state gate.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from attestation cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

device_projection_attestation.description: Complete origin-Station-signed device projection attestation. The detached proof signs the ak.device_projection_attestation_proof.v1 transcript; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.attested_at.

verified_device_projection.description: The device projection a client receives from its own authenticated Station on the self keys/query surface. The values are the ones the Station read out of the origin Station's verified device_projection_attestation; the row therefore carries no origin proof and no wrapper whose only job was to verify that proof, and a client MUST NOT treat this projection as portable evidence about the origin. account_id and device_id are not repeated here: they are the enclosing entry's account_id and the device_keys map key, and the returning Station MUST have checked that the verified attestation named exactly that pair before projecting it. attested_at is the origin's own observation instant, forwarded verbatim; together with authorized_generation_ref it is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref describe the closed shape of a usable row; a device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape rather than degraded into a partial projection.

device_status.description: This surface projects usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the projected status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: Origin observation instant of the verified projection, forwarded verbatim. MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh current-query cache deadline only, forwarded verbatim from the verified origin attestation. The returning Station MUST NOT extend it. Expiry does not revoke the signed device authorization or prohibit ordinary publication with verified cached evidence.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window, forwarded verbatim. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

device_key_view.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_response_body, the client-facing self surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. The row is the restricted typed result the client's own authenticated Station produces after it verified the origin Station's device_projection_attestation, so it carries the verified projection plus the prekey material and the signer_evidence_ref the client actually uses, and never the origin proof or its verification wrapper. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence the origin Station retained with its Station attester closure before the row was returned. It keeps pointing at that complete immutable evidence object: it is neither recomputed from this pruned projection nor an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the section 5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the self surface. The returning Station MUST have matched each verified attestation's account_id and device_id against this account_id and its enclosing device_id key before projecting the row. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

peer_device_key_view.description: Per-(account_id, device_id) entry in peer_keys_query_response_body, the Station-to-Station surface. account_id and device_id are the device_keys entry and map keys, not row fields. Every returned row is complete and attested: the origin Station signs the exact projection, so the requesting Station can verify the row without ever seeing PCR material. This is deliberately a different type from the client-facing device_key_view: the signed attestation is the object the requesting Station verifies, and a Station MUST NOT turn an unverified peer row into a client result by dropping its proof. A device whose generation is fenced, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

signer_evidence_ref.description: Exact account_device signer evidence retained with its Station attester closure before this row is returned. Its embedded attestation equals this row's attestation byte for byte; the ref is not an additional device-authority claim.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the Ã‚Â§5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_projection_attestation.description: Origin-Station signature over the authoritative device projection. Consumers read device_signing_key_did, hpke_key, device_status, device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref from the verified attestation. Its account_id and device_id MUST match the enclosing result group and device key; its signer MUST project onto account_id.station_id.

peer_query_account_device_entries.description: One device-key result group per exact AccountId on the Station-to-Station surface. Each signed device projection MUST match this account_id and its enclosing device_id key. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

account_device_algorithm_entries.description: One claim target group per exact AccountId. Entries MUST be sorted by RFC 8785 JCS AccountId bytes with no duplicate account identity.

query_account_device_selectors.description: Explicit account/device selectors sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of RFC 8785 JCS(account_id). Neither AccountId component may be inferred from the target service, caller session or another entry. Duplicate AccountIds MUST be rejected; use one entry containing all selected device_ids for that account. At most 16 accounts and 32 devices per account bound the local read and its cross-Station fan-out alike; an over-limit request fails whole and is never truncated.

query_failure.description: Closed non-enumerating failure row for the device directory read surfaces. device_result_unavailable covers absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets with one indistinguishable value. device_directory_unavailable states only that the requester's own Station could not obtain or verify a current attested projection this time; it never depends on target state and MUST NOT be rendered as an omitted row or an empty device set.

retry_after_ms.description: Only meaningful with device_directory_unavailable; a target-private failure MUST NOT carry it.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

device_generations.description: Current identity-root generation fence by exact AccountId. Fenced accounts or mismatched device generations expose no usable signing/HPKE/prekey material.

peer_keys_query_purpose.description: Declared use of the requested directory rows. The destination authorizes each purpose independently and MUST NOT clear the broadest one once.

peer_keys_relationship_basis.description: Closed relationship the requester asserts. The destination re-derives it from its own accepted state; a caller assertion never authorizes by itself. The contact branch deliberately carries no realm_id: a legitimate Contact needs no shared Realm.

peer_keys_query_request_body.description: Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read. It is the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target: the client asks its own Station, which authenticates itself with its own RFC 9421 service signature and never forwards a client SessionGrant, DPoP or any local bearer. Single authority, single hop, read only. Cross-Station single-use material stays with the MLS KeyPackage claim contract. Realm requester is restricted to MLS admission in its own Realm, with ordinary Account device targets only. The relationship realm_id MUST equal requester_actor_id.realm_actor_id.realm_id; current governor and both joined memberships are independently verified. Existing MLS capability, membership and policy rules remain unchanged.

request_id.description: Stable typed id the requesting Station mints for this fetch. The destination uses it only for correlation and rate limiting and keeps no durable ledger.

requester_account_id.description: Exact requesting account. Its station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and MUST NOT be inferred from a principal component, route or session.

requester_actor_id.description: Exact Realm requester; mutually exclusive with requester_account_id. The authenticated source is its verified current governing Station. No Bot-specific MLS permission or approval is introduced.

device_keys.description: Targets for this destination only: every account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Destination-Service-ID.

peer_keys_query_response_body.description: Verbatim origin-signed rows plus the closed non-enumerating failure shape. The destination does not add a response signature layer: every row carries the origin's own device_projection_attestation and signer_evidence_ref, and the requesting Station MUST verify them before projecting the restricted client-facing device_key_view. Echo request_id and the complete mutually exclusive requester branch exactly.

requester_actor_id.description: Exact Realm requester; mutually exclusive with requester_account_id. The authenticated source is its verified current governing Station. No Bot-specific MLS permission or approval is introduced.

oneOf.description: Native Device PUT requires exact immutable admission receipt bound to this complete packet and real first durable acceptance. Full native_source is atomically retained by Station and disclosed only through current-manager archive operations. Do not return native_source, sibling authorization originals/facts or unrelated scope names in this Device reply. A response bound to a native request cannot select the old Account reply branch. Exact replay preserves the original admission/accepted_at and does not increment archive_revision.

keys_backups_page.description: Bounded Account Station metadata page with the current accepted secret_storage backup-class pointer, independent of list filters. key-management.md section 7.6.1 fixes cursor and unknown-state semantics.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Closed exact single-object unlock intent. Branch authority, current validity, exact account/device/object, challenge and signature must all verify before durable allowance/budget/result commit. An identical retry by the same still-authorized holder returns the stored object without double charge.

keys_backups_issue_delete_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_delete_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (account_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_delete_challenge.description: Server-issued, durable, single-use delete challenge (TTL <= 300s). Every field is materialized by the service; the client echoes challenge_id in the DELETE body and every proof signs the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1, which embeds these exact values. Replay, expiry, path mismatch, or audience/service mismatch MUST fail closed.

challenge_id.description: Server-issued unique id of this challenge; echoed verbatim in the DELETE request body.

challenge.description: Exactly 32 CSPRNG octets encoded as canonical unpadded Base64URL. The service atomically binds and consumes this one unpredictable challenge with the complete existing operation context.

account_id.description: Exact account that owns the backup and challenge; both principal and Station components are signed by every delete proof.

audience.description: The service base origin this challenge is valid against; MUST match the origin the DELETE request is sent to.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

keys_backups_delete_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1. The service verifies the referenced challenge against the current caller/path/service, verifies the high-risk proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript, and consumes the challenge in the same transaction as the successful delete. A byte-identical network retry returns the stored terminal outcome without re-admitting the consumed challenge; the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

challenge_id.description: Exact echo of the server-issued challenge_id being consumed.

backup_active_series_state.description: Exact selected subject account and PCR basis. For agent_id list selection, account_id/control_realm_id belong to the Agent, while the authenticated controller and current custody are independently authorized; no caller/subject substitution.

oneOf.description: Exact current-device single-object challenge request. Idempotency binds current caller/device/generation, backup_id, request_id and the complete canonical request including subject/custody/content_history. Identical still-current replay returns identical challenge; changed intent is a conflict, never a widened or rebound challenge. Response echoes all optional scope fields exactly.

envelope_digest is SHA256(JCS(complete original KeyBackup including signature_proof.signature)); it is distinct from supersedes_digest. Bind it to the selected exact original and reject any complete-packet mutation, including signature-only mutation.

keys_backups_issue_unlock_challenge_requ.description: Native manager_ref/recovery_ref identify current requesting qualification; historical target packet original auth_binding and original author remain unchanged. recipient_ref selects the exact target original recipient declaration. Device challenge is current selected head only and binds current requester/authorization/generation/full actor/exact scope/complete envelope digest. Manager known exact-packet archive recovery remains independent of bulk inventory and requires current actor/scope/history qualification.

keys_backups_unlock_challenge.description: Shared-durable single-use current-device unlock challenge, TTL <= 300 seconds, scoped to authenticated account/device, exact backup/series/ciphertext, origin and service. All values are server materialized. Recovery-session unlock reuses its session challenge and MUST NOT call this operation.

challenge.description: Exactly 32 CSPRNG octets encoded as canonical unpadded Base64URL. The service atomically binds and consumes this one unpredictable challenge with the complete existing operation context.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

account_device_event_authorization.description: Exact pre-admission real Account Device source (Human or accepted Applet-managed), independently proven from native authorization. accepted_at is the original authorization Commit time; no target Commit exists yet. All fields enter the original Station attestation payload digest. Never present in directory/current-query evidence.

forward_device_projection_attestation_co.description: Forward-only closed same-cut real Account Device (Human or accepted Applet-managed) attestation. Original current projection fields plus a required exact Event-bound immutable authorization source. This is not a directory row or a grant.

account_id.description: Exact account owning the device projection. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto account_id.station_id; an attestation that verifies under any other Station key is not evidence about this account.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked or fenced device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Fresh authority_forward first-admission deadline: now MUST be earlier than expires_at; a new attempt MUST NOT reuse cached evidence. Exact already-accepted retry returns the original outcome before freshness checks. Original accepted historical verification uses original attested_at and MUST NOT reapply current TTL.

authorization_window.description: Exact source device authorization window. null expiry means no time limit. This is distinct from attestation cache freshness; ordinary publication uses this window and applicable revocation closures.

forward_device_projection_attestation.description: authority_forward real Account Device (Human or accepted Applet-managed) wrapper. Existing proof context and unique unsigned {attestation:core} projection; no new profile or proof context.

oneOf.description: realm_actor_id is a standard deepObject/explode=true query parameter. Both realm_actor_id[realm_id] and realm_actor_id[principal_id] are required together; percent-encode brackets. circle_id absent selects the Realm, present selects only that exact Circle. Raw typed parser rejects partial, duplicate, unknown or agent_id-mixed keys; no generic JSON-query decoder. Device actor/scope must exactly match signed metadata. Only current selected series current head, or empty for an empty series. Device cursor, limit, arbitrary series_id and backup_kind filters are forbidden. This gives ciphertext for exact same-scope continuation/current-root identity only, not archive private keys, plaintext roots or Event history. Sibling authors verify using their immutable first-PUT source, never today's Device directory.

Only current manager Service; same standard deepObject complete realm_actor_id encoding, no Device/Account, circle_id, series_id, backup_kind or agent_id. This all-scope view closes first-PUT custody inventory, not ordinary history enumeration.

envelope_digest.description: SHA256(RFC8785 JCS of the complete immutable original KeyBackup including signature_proof.signature and every actually present optional/x_* member). Never the signature-excluding predecessor supersedes_digest.

realm_actor_content_backup_admission.description: Immutable native first-PUT custody admission, fixed and signed only in the same durable transaction as exact ciphertext, original native Device authority and root index. envelope_digest hashes the complete canonical KeyBackup including its real producer proof. No EventId, RealmCommitId, fake stream position or boolean substitutes for this non-Event receipt. Validate the original Device public key against original authorization and verify actual Ed; current Device revocation does not change accepted-at validity. Signature uses the registered detached context and accepted_at; actual issuer/tenure and historical method must independently verify.

realm_actor_content_backup_source.description: Immutable original source returned only to qualified own publisher/current manager. device_authorization is the real original native Device authorize Event/Commit/private signer fact, not a receipt invented as a Commit. Its exact coordinates/key/generation and scope match admission. origin_resolution freezes complete issuer method-native history at accepted_at; verifier checks historical governance tenure and signature, not today's Device key or a new nonce-bound material response. No private archive key is disclosed. governance_history independently proves the actual historical governance tenure; origin_resolution alone only proves the Service method and is insufficient.

realm_actor_archive_backup_entry.description: Every native first-PUT packet, including packets with no successful business Event, losing Event CAS, response loss or failed first use. Full original ciphertext and source remain immutable; matching only backup_id or a local ACK journal is insufficient.

realm_actor_archive_series_entry.description: Every retained accepted native scope-series record and its exact real accepted source, not only the current primary. No raw Device signing/recipient private key appears. source is the immutable full original Event/Commit/fact exactly matching source_ref and record; no history-floor or current-selector bypass is inferred from a bare ref.

realm_actor_archive_recipient_entry.description: Every original accepted archive-recipient declaration required by any retained packet. declaration is immutable Event/Commit/necessary original fact. For a replacement installed by control.reset, recovery_begin MUST be the unique immutable exact accepted begin named by that reset, and its signed replacement matches. Otherwise recovery_begin is forbidden. No fresh material wrapper/nonce/clock is part of the manifest.

realm_actor_archive_inventory_manifest.description: Exact full all-scope native root namespace at one persisted private archive_revision, never a page or local-journal subset. Entry ordering is unsigned UTF8 lexical order of RFC8785 JCS typed identity keys: backup->[backup,backup_id], series->[series,effective_scope,record.active_series_id,record.series_pointer_version], recipient->[recipient,recipient_ref]. Reject duplicate typed identities even if other bytes differ. inventory_digest is SHA256(JCS(this full manifest)); no temporary nonce, current-material response, receipt-as-Event, arrival order or timestamp ordering is introduced.

realm_actor_archive_inventory_page.description: Manager-Service-only complete archive inventory. Current actor/manager/role, frozen full namespace cut, inventory digest, page position and authorization epoch bind the opaque cursor. Independent all-page collection verifies exact completeness and full manifest digest. Device/Account requests, circle/series filters, partial/mixed selectors, duplicate/unknown raw keys and stale/foreign cursor are refused. Native immutable admission receipts and original authorities are verified historically. Maximum canonical body4MiB; no private key is returned.

realm_actor_backup_governance_original.description: Original governance Event and accepting Commit. Require exactly the matching original producer fact iff Commit carries producer_signer_fact_digest; verify actual original producer Ed signature and authority chain. Missing, extra, invented or current-key-derived facts reject.

realm_actor_backup_governance_transition.description: One actual accepted governance change with its original old/new Service method-native evidence and dual-signed handoff. Verify exact Realm, consecutive generations, immutable Event/Commit IDs and handoff signatures; no local/private index is a Commit.

realm_actor_backup_governance_history.description: Immutable RealmId-bound genesis and consecutive accepted governance transitions through the exact native admission issuer tenure. This evidence is independently verified, including original producer proofs and Service methods at the corresponding historical times. Receipt realm_actor_id.realm_id, authority_ref, governance_generation, service_id and accepted_at must agree with that tenure. Never include nonce-bound current assertions, response timestamps, route hints or a current-material wrapper in the archive digest. Current caller authentication remains independently mandatory.

realm_actor_content_backup_handover_offe.description: Private existing manager offer/transfer channel only, not a new public operation. New Service signs this exact offer before old manager sends private material. It binds independently generated fresh X25519 next recipient, exact full actor/old manager/full inventory/revision/expiry and fresh nonce. Signature independently verifies the intended new Service and original method; an offered public key not yet accepted grants no native PUT or current recovery authority. Verify next keyAgreement against the accepted replacement actor DID declaration at manager change.

private_key_base64url.description: Secret raw 32-byte X25519 private key, owned only by the manager archive capability. SDK uses zeroizing SecretBytes and redacted Debug. Never serialize to an Event, ordinary DeviceStore, account data or public inventory. Derive the public key and require exact descriptor equality.

realm_actor_content_backup_private_recip.description: One original recipient private key and its immutable original accepted declaration identity. No current DID lookup or signature key conversion supplies this secret. Historical keys remain history-only and cannot authorize future PUT after replacement.

challenge_base64url.description: Fresh independent 32-byte CSPRNG challenge, secret and domain-bound to this actual HPKE transfer. SDK uses zeroizing SecretBytes/redacted Debug; never shared Event or ordinary DeviceStore.

realm_actor_content_backup_handover_plai.description: Complete private handover payload. Verify SHA256(JCS(offer))=offer_digest and full manifest inventory digest/revision/actor/manager equals offer; verify every immutable first-PUT source, original packet, scope-series and recipient original and all required private keys, rejecting missing/extra/duplicate recipient identities and key/public mismatches. handover_digest is SHA256(JCS(this exact plaintext including challenge)), never a page, local ACK subset or self-reported count. Preserve old original packet/declaration bytes. New manager durably imports the full validated custody and independent manager-only keys before any confirmation/acceptance signature.

realm_actor_content_backup_sealed_handov.description: Private existing offer/transfer channel, RFC9180 HPKE base mode only. Recipient is the fresh exact next_content_backup_recipient in independently verified new-Service offer. Info = UTF8("ak.realm_actor_content_backup_handover.v1\n") || JCS({realm_actor_id,manager_ref,new_service_id,offer_digest,inventory_digest}); offer_digest=SHA256(JCS(full signed offer)). AAD=JCS(full signed offer). Plaintext is the exact handover_plaintext. This independent domain never reuses daily Device Welcome keys, Ed keys, update seed, authoring KEK or ordinary KeyBackup HPKE info/AAD. No public endpoint, rootKeyBackup content item or shared Event carries this private object.

realm_actor_content_backup_handover_conf.description: New Service signs only after actual HPKE open, complete original/source/private-key validation and durable import. challenge_response_base64url is unpadded base64url HMAC-SHA256(key=decoded challenge, data=UTF8("ak.realm_actor_content_backup_handover_confirmation.v1\n") || JCS({offer_digest,inventory_digest,handover_digest})). Old manager verifies response with its original secret challenge, exact offer/cut and new-Service signature before submitting manager.change. The public manager acceptance separately signs the same inventory/handover digests and fresh recipient. This private challenge roundtrip is not a new public PoP algorithm, HTTP API or mathematical proof of physical retention; code and genuine import tests enforce the custody boundary. No private key or challenge is exposed publicly.

realm_actor_backup_metadata.description: Closed native current-head metadata only, projecting exact immutable accepted packet fields. No ciphertext, AEAD encapsulation, plaintext root, private archive key or complete-packet signature verification claim is included. admission.envelope_digest binds the complete original packet; obtain it only through the exact current-head challenge/unlock and verify the real original producer proof, HPKE AAD, complete packet/ciphertext digests and immutable original authorization. These metadata fields alone are not a signed full KeyBackup. Native metadata has no expires_at, including null; original first-PUT custody is not a time lease. created_at remains original packet time and is distinct from admission.accepted_at.

realm_actor_backup_head_entry.description: Exact current-head metadata plus minimum immutable first-PUT admission receipt only. No full native_source, sibling DeviceAuthorize Event, original fact, governance/DID bundle or unrelated Circle scope appears. Own Station independently verifies and durably retains full immutable source. Device validates the authenticated own-Station bound result and exact receipt/metadata actor, scope, original author key and complete packet digest; metadata is not full packet signature proof. No new receipt-signer network or governance discovery is allowed.

realm_actor_backup_unlock_response_body.description: Native Device-only complete current selected-series head and minimal immutable admission. No full native_source, sibling authorization original/fact, governance/DID bundle or unrelated Circle scope. Own Station verifies and retains full immutable accepted-at source before producing its authenticated current bound result. After verifying that own-Station result, Device checks receipt exact actor/scope/packet/ciphertext digest/authorization coordinates and uses receipt.device_public_key_base64url to independently verify the actual original KeyBackup Ed proof, including a sibling or revoked old author. Never substitute today's key, assume own authorization, query a new receipt signer network, or perform client governance discovery. Ciphertext/receipt alone grants no history/plaintext-root authority.

realm_actor_archive_unlock_response_body.description: Current-manager-only known exact archived packet and full immutable native_source for complete private historical verification/handover. Current manager qualification covers full target actor and independently current scope/history permission; original packet author/manager/recovery/recipient refs remain historical. Never return this branch to a native Device, even by optional flag. It can contain private sibling authorization scope lists and is not a Device DTO.

envelope_digest.description: SHA256(RFC8785 JCS of the complete immutable original KeyBackup including signature_proof.signature and every actually present optional/x_* member). Never the signature-excluding predecessor supersedes_digest.

realm_actor_content_backup_admission_sig.description: Exact closed unsigned projection of realm_actor_content_backup_admission: remove only the signature member, preserving every other actual host field, required member, order and constraint. This object is hashed by the registered detached proof transcript, not a complete signed host and not an Event. Reject signature, null, extra or omitted required members.

realm_actor_content_backup_handover_offe.description: Exact closed unsigned projection of realm_actor_content_backup_handover_offer: remove only the signature member, preserving every other actual host field, required member, order and constraint. This object is hashed by the registered detached proof transcript, not a complete signed host and not an Event. Reject signature, null, extra or omitted required members.

realm_actor_backup_series_head_response_.description: Current native selected-series head metadata and minimal immutable admission only, or zero items for empty selected series. No ciphertext, full native_source, sibling authorization originals, unrelated scope names, next_cursor, previous-series enumeration, archive key or plaintext root. Exact-head challenge/unlock returns the one complete packet plus minimal admission. Current manager archival recovery uses its independently qualified separate response.

keys_backups_list_response_body.description: Closed response union selected by authenticated role and registered query: original Account/Agent metadata Page, exact native Device current-head response, or current Manager complete archive inventory Page. No client flag may select a more privileged branch; native head is not a Page and has no cursor/has_more.

challenge.description: Exactly 32 CSPRNG octets encoded as canonical unpadded Base64URL. The service atomically binds and consumes this one unpredictable challenge with the complete existing operation context.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

realm_actor_backup_unlock_challenge.description: envelope_digest is SHA256(JCS(complete original KeyBackup including signature_proof.signature)); it is distinct from supersedes_digest. Bind it to the selected exact original and reject any complete-packet mutation, including signature-only mutation.

keys_backups_issue_unlock_challenge_resp.description: Closed issued-challenge response selected by authenticated request role. The Account/Agent branch preserves its original Challenge object. Native Device predecessor and current Manager archive roles use the separately closed native Challenge. Current requester manager/recovery/Device qualification remains separate from target original recipient and complete signed packet digest.
